clue.text: Deeply odd characters in improvised, melodramatic, European theatre

indicators.note: something improvised is made up on the spot, so the gathered letters are thrown into a new order
the odd-numbered letters of the word Deeply, first, third and fifth, are the ones taken

explanation.surface: A description of a bizarre, overacted, ad-libbed style of continental stage performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters in' Deeply gives DEL; with MELODRAMATIC and E, 'improvised' rearranges all sixteen letters. The surface describes the very genre, which relied on improvisation and stock characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Commedia dell'arte is the Italian form of improvised popular stage comedy with masked stock characters, so it is a kind of theatre.

clue.text: Club member served up half-eaten food for starters

parts.note: cud is food a cow has partly digested and chews again; for starters places it at the head of the answer

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word for a limb is written upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a member, a limb of the body

explanation.surface: Someone in a club is served a meal that is already half eaten as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club member' looks like one unit, a person in a society; 'Club' alone is the definition, a heavy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short thick stick used as a weapon, the same thing as a club.

clue.text: Runny centres of famous salted lozenges

indicators.note: the central letters of each of the three words famous, salted and lozenges are taken, two from each

explanation.surface: The gooey insides of well-known salty sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten means melted into liquid, so something molten is runny.

clue.text: Old thespian with name for introduction of rigour and accuracy

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another, the name letter swapping in

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in ex-wife
a thespian is an actor, here a female one, an actress

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, here the opening of rigour

explanation.surface: A retired actor brings in a name to bring discipline and precision to proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: EX + ACTRESS gives EXACTRESS; 'for' swaps its R, the 'introduction of rigour', for N. 'rigour and accuracy' reads like a pair of definitions, but rigour is only the source of R.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness and accuracy are synonyms, both meaning being precisely correct.

clue.text: Bury drug around mid-Dorset, scattered here and there

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body

indicators.note: around says the drug word wraps round the middle letters of the county

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, a drug

indicators.note: mid- picks the middle of the county name, its two central letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to hide drugs somewhere around the middle of Dorset, an English county, spread about in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the drug word round RS, the middle two letters of Dorset; 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Interspersed means placed at intervals among other things, distributed here and there.

clue.text: Satellite broadcast of enemy leader

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the words for the enemy leader are said aloud

parts.note: an enemy is a foe and a leader is a boss, so foe boss

explanation.surface: A satellite transmission carrying a hostile leader's message.
explanation.definitionFit: Phobos is the larger of the two moons of Mars, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Spotted killer, finally, through blurry image on camera

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of each of the five words through, blurry, image, on and camera

explanation.surface: A murderer is at last caught on a hazy CCTV image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted killer' reads as a murderer seen at last on film, but it defines the spotted hyena, a predator.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is a predatory African carnivore with a spotted coat, so a killer that is spotted.

clue.text: Barrister's opening material contains crucial evidence of fight?

indicators.note: the opening of the word Barrister's is its first letter
contains means the fabric word holds the word for crucial inside it

parts.note: lace is a decorative fabric, a material
key means crucial, as in a key witness

explanation.surface: A barrister opens the case and produces a decisive exhibit showing there was a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crucial evidence' looks like courtroom language, but 'evidence of fight?' is the definition; the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruised eye is the classic visible sign that someone has been in a punch-up.

clue.text: Ordinary way and a different way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Rd, short for road, is another kind of way

explanation.surface: A plain route and an alternative route.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal, usual, the regular kind, as ordinary does.

clue.text: See 1
State created by mapmaker, adjoining Alabama

indicators.note: adjoining tells us to set the mapmaker piece right beside the Alabama piece
created by says only the tail end of the word mapmaker is used to make the state

parts.note: Ala. is the traditional abbreviation for the US state Alabama

explanation.surface: A US state drawn up by a cartographer next to Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog reads it as a hidden word: put 'mapmaker' beside 'Alabama', as 'adjoining' asks, and the state runs across the join, KER from the end of mapmaker and ALA from the start of Alabama. The surface suggests an American state; the answer is Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerala is a state in south-west India, on the Malabar coast.

clue.text: An album of The Kinks that's impossible to get

indicators.note: kinks are twists, so the letters are twisted into a new order; the surface reads it as the rock band

explanation.surface: A record by the 1960s band the Kinks that is too rare to find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Kinks' looks like the band's name, but 'Kinks' is the signal to rearrange 'An album of The'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfathomable cannot be understood, so it is impossible to get in the sense of grasp.

clue.text: Do 70 keeping just within the limits

indicators.note: only the inside of the number word is kept, so its outermost letters at each limit are dropped

parts.note: the number written out in words is seventy

explanation.surface: Drive at seventy while staying just inside the speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do 70' reads as a driving speed; 'Do' is a noun for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is an informal word for a social function, an occasion such as a party.

clue.text: With loot missing was the manager fired?

parts.note: to have run something is to have managed it, so ran
sacked means dismissed from a job, fired

explanation.surface: Was the boss dismissed because stolen goods went missing?
explanation.definitionFit: A ransacked place has been plundered, searched and stripped, so its valuables have gone.

clue.text: Tuck's description as stated by main producer of fast food

indicators.note: by means the sea word stands beside the spoken phrase, here placed before it

parts.note: the main is the open sea, the deep

indicators.note: as stated means the phrase is spoken rather than written

parts.note: Friar Tuck, Robin Hood's companion, is traditionally a fat friar

explanation.surface: A school tuck shop described in terms of the biggest supplier of fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck' suggests British school snacks, a tuck shop, but it is Friar Tuck of the Robin Hood stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-fat fryer cooks chips and similar quick food by immersing it in hot oil, so it produces fast food.

clue.text: Gnome home acquired by enthusiast

indicators.note: acquired by means the enthusiast takes the home word into himself

parts.note: a fancier is an enthusiast, as in a pigeon fancier
in means at home

explanation.surface: A garden gnome fan buys a house for the ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' suggests a garden ornament, but the gnomes of Zurich are Swiss bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnomes of Zurich is a nickname for Swiss bankers, so a gnome is a financier.

clue.text: Lost civilisation identified by books I found in mountains

indicators.note: found in means the books and I sit inside the mountain range

parts.note: the Atlas are a mountain range in North Africa
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An archaeologist discovers a vanished culture by reading in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island civilisation said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: A good time for ladies of stature to absorb news

indicators.note: to absorb means the stature word soaks up the news letters inside it

parts.note: stature means height
N stands for new, so news, read as more than one new, gives two Ns

explanation.surface: Tall women catch up on the latest gossip during a fun evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a celebration for a bride-to-be and her female friends before the wedding.

clue.text: It's a challenging quest to love the health secretary

parts.note: to treasure someone is to love and cherish them
Jeremy Hunt was the UK Secretary of State for Health

explanation.surface: Adoring the government minister in charge of health is a tough undertaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure hunt is a game in which players solve clues to find a hidden prize, a quest.

clue.text: Tax collecting — it could show lack of seriousness

indicators.note: collecting means the tax word gathers the word it inside itself

parts.note: a levy is a tax or duty imposed by authority

explanation.surface: Gathering taxes is hardly a laughing matter, yet it might reveal frivolity.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is light-heartedness, treating serious matters without due gravity.

clue.text: Money obtained by cheesy setter on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the up means the word is written going upwards, read backwards

parts.note: rennet is the enzyme used to set milk into curds when making cheese

explanation.surface: Cash earned by a crossword compiler whose jokes are corny and improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests the crossword compiler; here it is what sets cheese. A tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound note or ten pounds, a sum of money.

clue.text: A code for life: manipulate a male until bored

parts.note: DNA carries the genetic code of living things
to use someone is to manipulate them

explanation.surface: A rule to live by: exploit a man until you lose interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam means to a tiresome, sickening extent, going on so long that everyone is fed up.

clue.text: Speak softly leaving club

indicators.note: leaving means the soft letter departs from the golf club word

parts.note: a putter is a golf club
p, piano, is the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Someone talks quietly as they walk out of a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a nightclub; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say something aloud, to speak words.

clue.text: Relative peace at last in Mediterranean resort

indicators.note: in means the last letter of peace goes inside the resort name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word peace

explanation.surface: A family member finally finds calm on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a brother's or sister's daughter, a family member.

clue.text: Clothing for dance contests in which tango replaces foxtrot

indicators.note: replaces means the tango letter takes the place of the foxtrot letter

parts.note: fights are contests, bouts
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Outfits for ballroom competitions where one dance is swapped for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tango' and 'foxtrot' look like dances, fitting the surface, but they are NATO alphabet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are close-fitting legwear worn by dancers, garments suited to dancing.

clue.text: Limbo dancing boy with violin — bar wobbly at the end

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the pooled letters are rearranged
bar means except, so a letter is barred from the word boy
at the end picks the final letter of the word wobbly

explanation.surface: A lad does the limbo carrying a fiddle while the bar shakes at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' and 'Limbo' together suggest the limbo pole; 'bar' means except, removing Y from BOY to leave BO for the anagram with VIOLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a state of being forgotten or neglected, as is oblivion.

clue.text: God's a performer of tricks, perhaps?

parts.note: the apostrophe s is taken as a letter s
a turn is a performer in a variety show, such as a magician doing tricks

explanation.surface: Is the Almighty just a conjuror?
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the Roman deity of agriculture and time, father of Jupiter.

clue.text: Shopper's item for carrying booze outside

indicators.note: outside means the drink word sits around the carrying item

parts.note: beer is booze
a tray is used to carry things such as drinks

explanation.surface: A shopper's bag holding alcohol on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' suggests someone buying goods; in British slang to shop someone is to inform on them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is to inform on them, so a shopper is one who betrays.
